stories.headline: Trumbull Arts Festival lineup set for Sunday on Town Hall Green
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Arts Festival returns Sunday, Sept. 27, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on the Town Hall Green with a free artisans market of 60+ local makers, a food-truck court, and a children’s creative tent. Gazebo acts include Tom Weber Children’s Music, Yoga for Everybody, Molly Bryce, and Mass Conn Fusion Quartet. Entry and parking are free; bring lawn chairs or blankets.

stories.headline: Judge: White House skipped due process before CNN / Politico media ban
stories.summary: Trump-appointed Judge Timothy Kelly said Wednesday the White House appears not to have followed required pre-deprivation notice before stripping CNN, MS NOW, and Politico press passes, but he did not rule immediately. DOJ called access a “privilege” and cited national-security reporting; the outlets and a 50-group amicus brief call it viewpoint discrimination. Trump vowed to appeal if he loses.

stories.headline: AP-KFF poll: rural voters still lean Trump, but pocketbook pain is rising
stories.summary: About half of rural registered voters say the economy is worse than when Trump returned to office, an AP-KFF survey finds, with groceries, gas, and healthcare topping worries. Trump still posts 48% rural approval — higher than adults overall — but down from 56% in an earlier rural poll, and only ~4 in 10 approve of his economic handling. Respondents often trust their own party more than they plan to switch sides.

stories.headline: AP Exclusive: ICE hides locator data for thousands with final removal orders
stories.summary: ICE quietly dropped detainees with final removal orders from its public online locator on Sept. 15, current and former officials told AP, leaving lawyers and families unable to find clients before deportation. Nearly 16,000 July bookings involved people with final orders; court-ordered exceptions remain at Adelanto and a few temporary sites. ICE neither confirmed nor denied the practice while saying final-order cases are deportation priorities.

stories.headline: Jets: Arian Smith out for season after ACL surgery; Onyemata sidelined weeks
stories.summary: HC Aaron Glenn confirmed Wednesday that WR Arian Smith had season-ending ACL surgery after Sunday’s Packers game, while DT David Onyemata’s core-muscle surgery will cost him several weeks. Mason Taylor, Minkah Fitzpatrick, Kene Nwangwu, and Kiko Mauigoa did not practice; Joseph Ossai is “very close.” The Jets also praised practice-squad QB Will Levis as a developmental add ahead of Detroit.

stories.headline: LEGO holiday wave: Icons Holiday House and Buddy the Elf lead Oct. 1 drop
stories.summary: The LEGO Group unveiled seven festive 2026 sets led by the 1,354-piece Icons Holiday House (11387) inspired by Jingle Bells, with Insiders early access Oct. 1 and general sale Oct. 4 at $119.99. Also arriving: Buddy the Elf, upscaled Mrs. Claus, ornaments, Santa’s sleigh, a countdown calendar, and a brick Christmas stocking. Private Insider shopping nights are set for mid-November.

stories.headline: LEGO confirms first Dragon Ball set is imminent — Adults Welcome teaser
stories.summary: Brickset reports LEGO’s social teaser confirms a Dragon Ball set is coming, showing seven Dragon Balls and an Adults Welcome logo that points to an 18+ model. Details are scarce beyond the IP reveal; fans widely expect a large Shenron Icons-style display build, with broader Dragon Ball play sets rumored for 2027. The confirmation follows months of licensing speculation after LEGO’s anime expansions.

stories.headline: Apple Watch Series 12: Health Sensing System, readiness score, Audio Intelligence
stories.summary: Apple’s Series 12 pairs a new Health Sensing System and S11 chip for higher-frequency heart rate and HRV sensing, a daily readiness score, and later Audio Intelligence features such as Live Rewind and Siri Recap. Everyday battery remains up to 24 hours with faster top-ups; aluminum, titanium, and new ceramic finishes start at $399. Availability began Sept. 18 alongside watchOS 27 and Siri AI.

stories.headline: Kaeden Korczak: Pens trade opened space to ‘reach more of my full potential’
stories.summary: Defenseman Kaeden Korczak, acquired from Vegas for Parker Wotherspoon, said his head was “spinning” when the call came — then settled into Pittsburgh’s sports town and camp. Assistant GM Jason Spezza cited upside, defensive solidity, and middle-aged roster fit; Korczak has been paired with Sam Girard and is studying Karlsson and Letang. The 25-year-old played a career-high 78 games last season and tasted a Stanley Cup Final run.

stories.headline: Matt Walsh calls Netflix ‘neck injury’ anniversary post ‘despicable’
stories.summary: Netflix UK & Ireland posted “Nearly did himself a neck injury” on Sept. 10 — the first anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s assassination by a neck shot — prompting Matt Walsh and others to call the timing intentional and urge cancellations. Netflix later said the caption referred to a Gentlemen wedding scene and denied any Kirk link. Critics note a year of online “neck injury” memes made the date hard to ignore.

stories.headline: Karen Woodall: Lighthouse Keeping maps repair after coerced child rejection
stories.summary: In a free essay, Karen Woodall describes six years building “Lighthouse Keeping” — a parent-mediated repair pathway for children forced to reject a parent after divorce. She argues labels and court battles obscured the child’s attachment trauma, and centers steady, right-action-at-the-right-time responses instead of rescue programs. Her book The Journey of the Alienated Child and a clinical handbook are due later in 2026.

stories.headline: Post–Labor Day USA parks window: Yosemite, Glacier, Arches drop timed entry
stories.summary: Yosemite, Glacier, and Arches dropped peak-season vehicle timed-entry systems for 2026, opening a quieter post–Labor Day shoulder season while many roads and trails stay open. Rocky Mountain kept timed entry through mid-October but offers classic elk-rut viewing from roads with distance rules. Shenandoah’s Skyline Drive remains reservation-free as early color begins at higher elevations.
